frames.observation: The exact Duskquill raven is readable in settled BirdFlySlow with a compact charcoal and indigo body, pale beak, amber eyes, and segmented wings and tail. Its authored surface and silhouette are distinct from the native crow art.
A wide BirdFlySlow downstroke spreads both long segmented wings while their sections remain connected to the body and preserve the intended angular silhouette.
At the end of the opening BirdFlySlow interval the raven holds a low, wide flight pose with both wings, tail, beak, and body coherent before the native attack begins.
During birdAttack2 the authored body lunges toward the hero with both broad wings still attached. The foreground hero and native Steadfast effect obscure part of the body at contact.
The birdAttack2 recovery pulls the raven away from the hero with the angular wing sections still attached. Combat effects and hero overlap limit fine inspection of the central and lower body.
The controller returns to BirdFlySlow with folded wings, a centered body, and the intended compact silhouette restored immediately after attack recovery.
A later BirdFlySlow sample retains the coherent raven silhouette, though strong camera motion blur prevents a fine texture or edge assessment in this exact frame.
The ordinary no-focus attack begins with the exact Duskquill renderer settled in BirdFlySlow at 58 HP. Both wings and the tail are visible and aligned.
At the native Damaged trigger boundary the bright impact sphere and foreground hero almost entirely obscure the raven. This frame establishes gameplay timing but provides little deformation evidence.
During BirdDamage the raven recoils above the target tile with its body and folded wing sections connected. The ordinary 8-damage label is visible as HP resolves to 50.
The target finishes the damage response at 50 HP with the authored raven still coherent beside the foreground hero as feather particles clear.
The native AttackCrit action begins from a recovered 50 HP flight pose with both wings spread evenly and the body centered between them.
At birdAttack2 contact the wide wings, body, legs, and beak remain connected in a readable attack silhouette. The bright ground effect limits fine inspection behind the model.
The raven retreats from its native counterattack with both folded wings and tail still aligned while the Pierced result remains on screen.
The separate explicit KillSingle fixture begins from a settled BirdFlySlow pose at 50 HP with the exact raven visible and coherent.
At the explicit fixture impact, the hero, bright sphere, and feather effect obscure the raven. This frame supports trigger timing and is not used for a detailed mesh-shape claim.
BirdDeath has begun and the raven is falling behind the hero with its wings still connected. Dense feather particles and the 1000-damage label limit surface inspection.
The animated death has placed the raven on the floor in a coherent spread-wing pose. Its body and both wings remain visible behind the hero as particles dissipate.
The exact model remains visible in its spread-wing BirdDeath floor pose after the combat objective completes. Camera focus softens fine edges but the whole silhouette remains readable.

The same animated floor pose is still visible behind the native loot overlay at the final requested frame. The overlay and depth blur prevent detailed surface inspection, and no lifetime beyond this sampled window is claimed.

requirements: All 20 referenced original PNGs were inspected at original resolution before assigning this reviewed status.
The ordinary no-focus gameplay claim is limited to the same-target HP change from 58 to 50; the separate KillSingle fixture at 50 HP is not ordinary lethal evidence.
The death claim is a completed 120-frame BirdDeath animation with m_DoRagdoll=false and zero rigid bodies; it is animated death evidence, not ragdoll proof.
The exact enCrow renderer remained active, enabled, and visible in all 360 retained frames; selected originals support visual conclusions only for their sampled views.
Native combat UI, effects, foreground hero overlap, loot overlay, depth blur, camera movement, and the small flying scale limit fine surface inspection.
